_comment: Turn the joint-limit gate on, keeping everything else at the shipped defaults.
Design: docs/2026-10-22-j5-overtravel-kinematics-gate-design.md; the staged plan this
switch now belongs to is docs/tmp/upgrade-plan.md.
scanplan plan --station input/station_fixed.json --config configs/robot_gate.json --out output/robot
What changes when this is on:
* a pose the arm cannot hold with joint_margin_deg to spare is rejected BEFORE the
selection, so the reported coverage describes poses that can actually be commanded;
* every sweep is WALKED as a straight Cartesian line holding its starting branch, and
one that runs out of branch halfway is dropped instead of delivered - this is the check
whose absence let X10290 be written, imported and then die at J2 mid-segment;
* the connector becomes a single joint move from a sweep's end to the next sweep's
start, with no retract corner and no CONFIG, so the retract/reorient points that held
all seven unsolvable points of the old 99% run no longer exist;
* the program mixes representations: scan starts and transition points are written as
J1..J6 and reached with J, scan ends stay Cartesian and are reached with L;
* the report grows a `kinematics` block with the J5 distribution, the branch histogram,
the worst joint step, and the connector route mix with its refusal reasons.
Measured on the real station, seed 7, --fast, --coverage-target none, 2026-10-29:
gate off  99.04% coverage, 32 points, 11 transition points
gate on   91.25% coverage, 59 points,  2 transition points, pool ceiling 91.81%
connector {'J-direct': 51, 'L2-retract-through': 6}, refused {'collision': 10, ...}
That is 99.4% of the pool ceiling delivered, against 75.6% before the connector rewrite.
The 91.25 rather than 91.51 is the price of robot.wrist_flip_policy = 'T', which is not
optional: the program's CONFIG can only ask for that branch.
Two things about this switch that are easy to get wrong:
G1 `enabled=false` is the regression profile, not a recommendation. It reproduces the
pre-2026-10-22 result exactly, which is why the shipped config keeps it off.
G2 the DELIVERY check in `<NAME>_frame.json` does not read this switch. It always runs,
with its own Robot and its own cache, because the switch describes the planning
sieve and never whether the arm can fly the file.
Before using a gate-on run as an acceptance criterion, confirm the two site gaps in
docs/tmp/upgrade-plan.md section 11.3: the CONFIG letters the controller expects on a
Cartesian point, and `robot.max_rot_deg_per_mm`, which is a measured lower bound (0.669)
rather than a limit and now only constrains the retract fallback.
